> 民不畏威，則大威至.

One character in this chapter breaks open the whole idea of authority.

## 威 is a mother-in-law with an axe

威: 姑也. From 女 and 戌.

姑 is the mother-in-law — and 說文 cites the Han statutes as evidence: 漢律曰：婦告威姑. A wife suing her mother-in-law is recorded as suing the 威姑.

So the oldest sense of 威 is: the one seated in the main hall.

A woman with an axe in her hand. She does not speak. The whole household is careful around her.

That is the prototype of 威 — not hitting anyone, but sitting there so the room does not raise its voice.

## 民不畏威，則大威至

The picture is now specific: the one seated in the hall is no longer feared.

A household that has reached that point is not waiting to be attacked. It is already coming apart — and 大威至 is not a bigger punishment arriving from outside. It is the arrival of the only kind of force that works on people who have stopped being afraid.

## 無狎其所居，無厭其所生

狎: a dog too familiar — the 犬 with 甲, the closeness that has lost its boundary.

Do not crowd the place they live. Do not press the life they live.

厭, as in chapter 66, is 笮 — to press.

The two prohibitions are both about proximity and weight: don't stand so close that their dwelling has no room, don't put weight on the thing that keeps them alive.

## 夫唯不厭，是以不厭

Two 厭's, one character.

Not "because he is not disgusted, he is not disliked." It is: because he does not press, they do not feel pressed.

Pressure and the feeling of pressure are the two ends of a single act.

## 自知不自見，自愛不自貴

見 is to make visible — to display. 貴: 物不賤也, from 貝: 貴 is price.

So the pair is exact:

- 自知 not 自見 — knows himself, does not put himself on display.
- 自愛 not 自貴 — holds himself dear, does not put a price on himself.

One is about visibility, one about valuation. 自愛 is not selling yourself cheap; 自貴 is setting your own price high.

## 故去彼取此

Remove that, take this: remove the display and the price; keep the knowing and the holding-dear.

## Why this follows 71

71: fix the scoring, because a false call propagates.
72: and the same failure at the scale of a household — the one who displays and prices himself has already stopped being feared, and does not know it.

Both are about a report that has drifted from the facts, one inside the person and one in the room.

## A test

Take the place where you have authority. Ask whether the people there are quiet because you are steady, or because they are careful. The difference is 威 versus 畏, and it is usually visible in whether anyone brings you bad news.
